rules.rule: College degrees ARE present — 55.2% bachelor's or higher is confirmed
Society is PRE-neuron chemistry — decisions are behavioral, not pharmacological
The "newness illusion" (confusing purchase date with build date) is systemic
IQ correlates with property lifecycle awareness and retirement preparedness
Lender geography (45% out-of-state) means capital decisions are remote
Property age histogram peaks at 1980-1999 — most stock is aging silently
Three society ages (Tobacco, University, Tech) explain the IQ shift
Health outcomes correlate inversely with newness illusion strength
Retirement savings deficit correlates with newness illusion magnitude
Pre-neuron chemistry society cannot optimize dopamine/cortisol responses to property

suggestions.suggestion: Citizens should be educated on BUILD DATE vs PURCHASE DATE distinction
Retirement calculators should include deferred-maintenance shock modeling
IQ-stratified financial literacy programs would reduce savings gaps
Local lenders (35% market share) should offer age-of-structure awareness tools
Future neuron-chemistry-aware society will render newness illusion obsolete
Property tax assessments should visually display structure age prominently

pre-neuron-chemistry-notes.note: Society operates on behavioral psychology, not receptor-level optimization
Serotonin, dopamine, cortisol, and oxytocin drive property decisions unconsciously
IQ is measured but not pharmacologically enhanced or modulated
Intelligence is perceived as fixed rather than chemically tunable
The "nest instinct" (oxytocin) makes purchase = bond, creating newness illusion
Retirement anxiety (cortisol) is treated as normal rather than chemically manageable
Dopamine novelty bias makes new purchases feel "new" regardless of build year
A post-neuron-chemistry society would: medicate illusions, optimize savings behavior, and treat property decisions as pharmacologically-informed actuarial computations
